## Summary

I wrote the design-discussion document for the `rip-out-consus-coupling` epic at:

`/Users/mdostal/Documents/work/pantheon/minerva/.pHive/epics/rip-out-consus-coupling/docs/design-discussion.md`

It's 471 lines, following the required structure exactly: §0 NORTH STAR prelude (no PRIOR DECISIONS, per the empty kg_why query), §1–§8 in order, ending with `SCOPE_CLASS: single-epic`. Line count runs a bit above the ~250-350 guideline but lands close to the in-repo precedent for a comparably-scoped epic (`fix-startrun-heimdall-routing`'s design-discussion.md is 422 lines).

Key positions taken in the doc, per the operator's actual question ("what is left of Minerva at the end"):

- **§1**: The generic `waiting_on_human`/`submitAnswers` pause-resume mechanism (AD-5) is what's left — it was always the real product; Consus was an unconditional side-effect bolted on top, never load-bearing.
- **§3(a)-(c)**: Mandatory, no-debate rip-out of the core-woven coupling (`dispatch.ts`, `kickoff-engine.ts`'s unconditional call, `run-manager.ts`'s types, the 4 dedicated `consus-*.ts` modules) and closing (not just gating) `plan-runner.ts`'s unconditional Consus-surfacing block, plus a clean CLI-surface removal in `bin/minerva.ts`.
- **§3(d)**: Took a real stance — `bin/minerva-plan.ts` and `bin/ideate-to-consus.mjs` may stay, grounded in the operator's own "process piece or a flag" framing, with the one loose end (hardcoded `pollConsusForAnswers: true`) closed by making it a compile-time forcing function.
- **§3(e)**: Multica consolidation ruled out of this epic's scope (already flag-gated, different problem than the one that broke 20 tests), flagged explicitly as Open Question 2 rather than silently dropped.
- **§7**: A concrete VERIFICATION PLAN including the operator's explicit live-PoC ask — re-running the pause/resume test with a real Consus service reachable, confirming status stays `waiting_on_human`, never `awaiting-consus`.

No implementation code was written — this is the design-discussion artifact only.
